[LLM] Arcane GitOps: non-admin PUT on /api/customize/git-repositories/{id} followed by /test, /branches, or /files within 5 min (CVE-2026-45625 cr Actions on Objectives High
Detects the signature exploit primitive for CVE-2026-45625: a PUT against an Arcane git-repositories management endpoint (URL pivot) followed within seconds by a /test, /branches, or /files call on the same repository ID from the same authenticated principal. This sequence forces Arcane to decrypt the stored PAT/SSH key and present it to the URL the caller just set — a one-step cleartext exfiltration. Rationale: Anchors on the exact endpoint paths and HTTP methods called out in the advisory (`PUT /api/customize/git-repositories/{id}` to pivot the URL, then `POST /test` or `GET /branches` or `GET /files` to force the credential decrypt-and-send). The 5-minute correlation window mirrors the advisory's described one-step chain. A normal admin save-then-walk-away workflow does not produce a sub-5-minute PUT→test cycle on the same repo ID. Cross-checked against the GitHub Advisory (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7h26-hg47-p9hx) and Arcane API reference (https://getarcane.app/api-reference). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7h26-hg47-p9hx • https://github.com/getarcaneapp/arcane • https://getarcane.app/api-reference

[LLM] Arcane backend host outbound Git/HTTPS to non-allowlisted host on port 22/443 (CVE-2026-45625 credential sink) Command & Control Medium
Detects the network-side smoking gun of CVE-2026-45625 exploitation: the Arcane backend process making an outbound git-protocol connection (HTTPS or SSH) to a host that is not in the organization's approved Git server allow-list. After the attacker pivots a repo URL, go-git sends `Authorization: Basic <base64(user:PAT)>` in its first reference-discovery request to the attacker host on the next /test, /branches, or /files call — so this egress is the cleartext-credential transfer. Rationale: The advisory states Arcane's go-git client transmits `Authorization: Basic base64(username:token)` to the configured URL on the first ref-discovery call. The Arcane process is the only legitimate initiator of outbound git traffic from the Arcane host; any destination outside the org's known Git providers is suspicious by definition. CIDRs taken from GitHub's published meta endpoint (https://api.github.com/meta) — replace ArcaneHosts/CIDRs with the actual org-specific allow-list and Arcane device tags. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7h26-hg47-p9hx • https://api.github.com/meta • https://github.com/getarcaneapp/arcane

[LLM] Arcane GitOps: DELETE /api/customize/git-repositories/{id} by non-admin principal (CVE-2026-45625 DoS / post-exfiltration cleanup) Actions on Objectives High
Detects DELETE requests against Arcane's git-repositories management endpoints, which the advisory calls out as a denial-of-service primitive (`DELETE every repo for DoS on the GitOps pipeline`) and which an attacker may also use to wipe evidence after an exfil run. On a patched system this endpoint is admin-only; pre-patch it is reachable by any authenticated role. High-fidelity because DELETE on production GitOps source-of-truth configs should be rare and operator-initiated. Rationale: Anchored on the exact endpoint + method named in the advisory's `DELETE /customize/git-repositories/{id} lets any user wipe production repository configurations`. Excludes `/sync` (the one endpoint that does enforce admin) to avoid noise. DELETE on production GitOps source-of-truth is operationally rare and aligns with either the DoS scenario or the article's optional-cleanup step (`DELETE every repo for DoS on the GitOps pipeline`). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7h26-hg47-p9hx
ATT&CKT1485 T1531 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where RequestMethod =~ "DELETE"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"/api/customize/git-repositories/[^/?]+/?($|\?)"
| extend RepoId = extract(@"/api/customize/git-repositories/([^/?]+)", 1, RequestURL)
| extend User = coalesce(SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestClientApplication)
| summarize Hits = count(), DeletedRepos = make_set(RepoId), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SrcIPs = make_set(SourceIP)
          by User
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| where Hits >= 1
| order by Hits desc, LastSeen desc

How to Reduce Phishing Exposure Before It Turns into Business Disruption

The Hacker News
2026-05-18 9 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

What happens when a phishing email looks clean enough to pass through security, but dangerous enough to expose the business after one click? That is the gap many SOCs still struggle with: the attacks that leave teams unsure what was exposed, who else was targeted, and how far the risk has spread. Early phishing detection closes that gap. It helps teams move from uncertainty to evidence faster,

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process

status: experimental
description: |

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20131")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-20131")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-20131")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-20131")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access

    category: process_access
    product: windows

    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"

[LLM] n8n Git node CLI argument injection (CVE-2026-44790) — git child of node with --upload-pack/--receive-pack/-c core.sshCommand Exploitation High
Hunts the specific CWE-88 argument-injection exploitation path in n8n's Git node Push operation. An authenticated workflow editor injects CLI flags into the git invocation, causing the n8n Node.js worker to spawn git with attacker-controlled --upload-pack=/--receive-pack=/-c core.sshCommand= flags that read arbitrary files or trigger code execution. Rationale: Cross-checked CWE-88 argument-injection mechanics (GHSA-9g95-qf3f-ggrw and GHSA-57g9-58c2-xjg3) which confirm --upload-pack/--receive-pack/-c core.sshCommand= as the concrete injection vectors. The article names the Git node Push operation explicitly, and n8n's runtime is Node.js so the parent/child invariant (node→git with those flags) is high-fidelity — these flags should never appear in benign n8n Git node usage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/88.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
ATT&CKT1059 T1190 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","n8n","n8n.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("git","git.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--upload-pack=", "--receive-pack=", "core.sshCommand", "--exec=")
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)-c\s+core\.sshCommand"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","n8n")
| where TargetProcessName endswith "git" or TargetProcessName endswith "git.exe"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--upload-pack=","--receive-pack=","core.sshCommand","--exec=")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)-c\s+core\.sshCommand"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash
title: n8n Git Node CLI Argument Injection (CVE-2026-44790)
id: c8f3d2a1-7e64-4b9c-8f21-3a5d7c9e1b40
status: experimental
description: Detects n8n Git node argument injection via the Push operation where node/n8n spawns git with attacker-controlled CLI flags (--upload-pack=, --receive-pack=, -c core.sshCommand=) enabling arbitrary file read and code execution per CVE-2026-44790.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/ivanti-fortinet-sap-vmware-n8n-patch.html
  - https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/n8n'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/git'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--upload-pack='
      - '--receive-pack='
      - 'core.sshCommand'
      - '--exec='
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_args
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate n8n Git node workflows that legitimately use --upload-pack with a trusted binary (rare; investigate value)
  - Internal CI scripts shelling git through Node.js orchestrators with bespoke flags
level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) (@process.executable.path:(*/git OR */git.exe) OR @Image:(*/git OR *\\git.exe OR *\\Git.exe)) (@process.parent.executable.path:(*/node OR */n8n OR *\\node.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\n8n.exe)) (@process.command_line:(*--upload-pack=* OR *--receive-pack=* OR *core.sshCommand* OR *--exec=*) OR @CommandLine:(*--upload-pack=* OR *--receive-pack=* OR *core.sshCommand* OR *--exec=*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\git(\.exe)?$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/git$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|n8n)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("--upload-pack=|--receive-pack=|core\.sshCommand|--exec=", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] n8n Node.js worker spawning interactive shell — RCE chained from prototype-pollution CVEs (42231/42232/44789/44791) Installation High
Hunts the post-exploitation tell of the four n8n prototype-pollution RCEs: the n8n worker (node process) spawning an interactive shell or known reverse-shell pattern. Legitimate n8n workflows execute via Function/Code nodes inside the Node.js VM and should not be spawning /bin/sh, bash -i, cmd.exe or PowerShell as children of the n8n process tree. Rationale: All four prototype-pollution CVEs (42231 xml2js webhook handler; 42232 XML node; 44789 HTTP Request node pagination; 44791 XML node bypass) terminate at the same observable: Node.js child_process spawn of a shell/interpreter for arbitrary command execution. Targeting that single behavioural choke point covers all four CVEs without needing to model each pollution gadget. Cross-checked with the article's explicit statement that each chain results in 'remote code execution on the n8n host'. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1321.html

[LLM] Vulnerable n8n / Ivanti Xtraction / FortiAuthenticator / FortiSandbox / SAP / VMware Fusion inventory — exposure surface map Reconnaissance High
Surface every host running an n8n, Ivanti Xtraction, FortiAuthenticator, FortiSandbox, SAP S/4HANA, SAP Commerce Cloud, or VMware Fusion build affected by the patch round. Drives patching prioritisation and identifies the blast radius before the article's CVEs are weaponised in the wild. Rationale: Article enumerates 11 distinct CVEs across 5 vendors with concrete fixed-version strings (e.g. n8n 1.123.43 / 2.20.7 / 2.22.1; FortiAuthenticator 6.5.7 / 6.6.9 / 8.0.3; FortiSandbox 4.4.9 / 5.0.2; VMware Fusion 26H1). TVM tables are the only direct way to map all of them at once without N separate process-level UCs that would fire only post-exploitation. Datadog/Falcon/Splunk left empty because TVM data lives in Defender XDR; equivalent vulnerability inventory in those platforms requires vendor-specific shippers outside the article's scope. Cross-checked against: • https://forums.ivanti.com/s/article/Security-Advisory • https://fortiguard.fortinet.com/psirt • https://support.broadcom.com/security-advisory

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents

| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MiniPlasma Windows 0-Day Enables SYSTEM Privilege Escalation on Fully Patched Systems

The Hacker News
2026-05-18 13 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have discovered four new npm packages containing information-stealing malware, one of which is a clone of the Shai-Hulud worm open-sourced by TeamPCP. The list of identified packages is below - chalk-tempalte (825 Downloads) @deadcode09284814/axios-util (284 Downloads) axois-utils (963 Downloads) color-style-utils (934 Downloads) "One of the packages (chalk-tempalte)

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Install of typosquatted Shai-Hulud copycat npm packages (chalk-tempalte / axois-utils / color-style-utils / @deadcode09284814/axios-util)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Phantom Bot persistence registration by node/npm context (axois-utils GoLang implant survives package deletion) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection or DNS to Shai-Hulud copycat C2 (lhr.life subdomains / 80.200.28.28:2222) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] node/npm process reading SSH private keys or cloud credential files (Shai-Hulud infostealer behavior) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Outbound connection or DNS to Shai-Hulud copycat C2 (lhr.life subdomains / 80.200.28.28:2222) Command & Control High
Hunts the four named C2 endpoints from the May 2026 Shai-Hulud copycat npm campaign: three localhost.run tunnel subdomains (87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life, b94b6bcfa27554.lhr.life, edcf8b03c84634.lhr.life) and the raw IP:port 80.200.28.28:2222 used by @deadcode09284814/axios-util. Any endpoint resolving or connecting to these IOCs almost certainly installed one of the four malicious packages. Rationale: Three of the four named C2 domains and one IP:port are explicitly listed in the article's IOC table and corroborated by BleepingComputer, TheRegister, and OX Security. lhr.life is the localhost.run tunnel service - already classified as suspicious by URLert when used for tunnel-hosted content. The three subdomains are operation-specific (random-hex) so false positives are negligible. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/leaked-shai-hulud-malware-fuels-new-npm-infostealer-campaign/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/05/18/shai-hulud-copycat-hits-another-npm-package/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/new-actors-deploy-shai-hulud-clones-teampcp-copycats-are-here/ • https://www.urlert.com/domains/lhr.life
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.002 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let C2Domains = dynamic(["87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life","b94b6bcfa27554.lhr.life","edcf8b03c84634.lhr.life"]);
let C2IP = "80.200.28.28";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (RemoteIP == C2IP and RemotePort == 2222)
    or RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life","b94b6bcfa27554.lhr.life","edcf8b03c84634.lhr.life"]);
let C2IP = "80.200.28.28";
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where Name has_any (C2Domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Source="DnsEvents"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where DestinationIP == C2IP and DestinationPort == 2222
     or RequestURL has_any (C2Domains)
     or DestinationHostName has_any (C2Domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where DstIpAddr == C2IP and DstPortNumber == 2222
     or DstHostname has_any (C2Domains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, Source="ImNetworkSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Install of typosquatted Shai-Hulud copycat npm packages (chalk-tempalte / axois-utils / color-style-utils / @deadcode09284814/axios-util) Delivery High
Detects execution of npm/yarn/pnpm with any of the four named malicious package names from the May 2026 campaign. The package list is fixed and the names include a deliberate typo (chalk-tempalte not chalk-template; axois-utils not axios-utils) so the regex is high-fidelity. Rationale: The four package names are explicitly enumerated in the article's IOC summary and confirmed by BleepingComputer/OX Security write-ups. The typosquat misspellings (tempalte/axois) make false positives effectively zero - no legitimate project depends on these strings. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/leaked-shai-hulud-malware-fuels-new-npm-infostealer-campaign/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/new-actors-deploy-shai-hulud-clones-teampcp-copycats-are-here/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/05/18/shai-hulud-copycat-hits-another-npm-package/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","npx.cmd","node.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (MalPackages)
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (MalPackages)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountUpn,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let MalPackages = dynamic(["chalk-tempalte","axois-utils","color-style-utils","@deadcode09284814/axios-util"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe","npx.cmd")

(ImProcessCreate

[LLM] node/npm process reading SSH private keys or cloud credential files (Shai-Hulud infostealer behavior) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the credential-harvesting behavior of the Shai-Hulud clone in chalk-tempalte and the unobfuscated infostealer in @deadcode09284814/axios-util: a postinstall node.exe child reading ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud/, ~/.azure/, .npmrc, and known crypto wallet paths. Pivots on InitiatingProcessFileName=node.exe / npm touching credential-shaped paths. Rationale: The article describes both chalk-tempalte (Shai-Hulud clone) and @deadcode09284814/axios-util as harvesting SSH keys, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, and env vars. The detection pivots on the postinstall-spawned node.exe touching multiple credential paths in a short window - high-fidelity because legitimate node packages rarely read >=2 distinct cred locations. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/leaked-shai-hulud-malware-fuels-new-npm-infostealer-campaign/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/new-actors-deploy-shai-hulud-clones-teampcp-copycats-are-here/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let CredPaths = dynamic([
  "\\.ssh\\id_rsa","\\.ssh\\id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519",
  "\\.aws\\credentials","/.aws/credentials",
  "\\.config\\gcloud","/.config/gcloud",
  "\\.azure\\accessTokens","\\.azure\\azureProfile",
  "\\.npmrc","/.npmrc",
  "wallet.dat","keystore","metamask","electrum"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName has_any (CredPaths)
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","devenv.exe","webstorm64.exe","idea64.exe")
    or ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| summarize PathsTouched = dcount(FolderPath), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Sample = make_set(FolderPath, 10)
        by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where PathsTouched >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
let CredPaths = dynamic(["\\.ssh\\id_rsa","\\.ssh\\id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","\\.aws\\credentials","/.aws/credentials","\\.config\\gcloud","/.config/gcloud","\\.azure\\accessTokens","\\.npmrc","/.npmrc","wallet.dat","keystore","metamask"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths) or TargetFileName has_any (CredPaths)
| summarize PathsTouched = dcount(TargetFilePath), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Sample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where PathsTouched >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc

description: Detects node.exe / npm / yarn / pnpm processes accessing or modifying SSH private keys, AWS/GCP/Azure credential files, .npmrc tokens, or known crypto wallet artefacts - the Shai-Hulud infostealer credential-harvest pattern.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/four-malicious-npm-packages-deliver.html
  - https://www.ox.security/blog/new-actors-deploy-shai-hulud-clones-teampcp-copycats-are-here/

logsource:

detection:

      - '\yarn.cmd'

[LLM] Phantom Bot persistence registration by node/npm context (axois-utils GoLang implant survives package deletion) Installation Medium
Targets the axois-utils-specific behavior - a GoLang Phantom Bot binary dropped to disk and registered for autostart by a postinstall-spawned node.exe / npm process. The article notes persistence 'survives package deletion' which means an autostart entry (Run key, scheduled task, service, or startup folder shortcut) outside the node_modules tree. Rationale: The article specifically calls out axois-utils as delivering a GoLang Phantom Bot with persistence 'that survives package deletion' - meaning autostart entries outside node_modules. A node.exe / npm.cmd process writing a Run key or creating a service/scheduled task is intrinsically anomalous since legitimate package installs don't register OS-level persistence. Cross-checked against: • https://www.ox.security/blog/new-actors-deploy-shai-hulud-clones-teampcp-copycats-are-here/ • https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/05/18/shai-hulud-copycat-hits-another-npm-package/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1053.005 T1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let NodeProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd"]);
let AutostartKeys = dynamic([
  "\\CurrentVersion\\Run",
  "\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce",
  "\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Run",
  "\\Services\\",
  "\\Image File Execution Options\\"
]);
(
  DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (NodeProcs)
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (NodeProcs)
  | where RegistryKey has_any (AutostartKeys)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
            InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName,
            RegistryValueData, Source="Registry"
)
| union
(
  DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (NodeProcs)
  | where FileName in~ ("schtasks.exe","sc.exe","reg.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create","create binPath","reg add","\\Run","Register-ScheduledTask","New-ScheduledTask")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
            InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine,
            RegistryKey="", RegistryValueName="", RegistryValueData=FileName, Source="ProcessSpawn"
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let NodeProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd"]);
let AutostartKeys = dynamic(["\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce","\\Services\\","\\Image File Execution Options\\"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any (NodeProcs)
  | where RegistryKey has_any (AutostartKeys)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, Source="ImRegistryEvent"),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any (NodeProcs)
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("schtasks.exe","sc.exe","reg.exe","powershell.exe")
  | where CommandLine has_any ("/create","reg add","\\Run","Register-ScheduledTask","binPath=")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername=Account, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=CommandLine, RegistryKey="", RegistryValue="", RegistryValueData=NewProcessName, Source="SecurityEvent4688")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the

        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["165fa92d237fd017c227d00da06ab788212a62be94bf61e95df2d22d00377ef2", "7d0ae79fdb1e9968f3323a3712b624643a782ba3efb2cf3a2cb9c4c5513cea30", "308b15c023088a7188dea4ef609010ac2493eb4c365b103053d7621a9ca5b935", "9e380ec88d3ccf3929e1a104e3b868d4d7b59ca189a8a431a54e9f3357dfdd81", "d1c9e3f296ee9f7d5032f73f9c504cede50334bc14c394055fd5cb9c3a6e08b3", "ffba9bdd6793edd5b38e12900252c1813a693f59c25af51c3b658cf3f27b6162"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)

                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/

    - attack.credential-access

level: high

        | where SHA256 in~ ("9a10e1faa86a5d39417cae44da5adf38824dfb9a16432e34df766aa1dc9e3525", "07c69fc33271cf5a2ce03ac1fed7a3b16357aec093c5bf9ef61fbfa4348d0529", "8fcb4d3d4df61719ee3da98241393779290e0efcd88a49e363e2a2dfbc04dae9", "de584703c78a60a56028f9834086facd1401b355", "dbe51eabebf9d4ef9581ef99844a2944", "0ff6abe0252d4f37a196a1231fae5f26", "410eddfc19de44249897986ecc8ac449") or SHA1 in~ ("9a10e1faa86a5d39417cae44da5adf38824dfb9a16432e34df766aa1dc9e3525", "07c69fc33271cf5a2ce03ac1fed7a3b16357aec093c5bf9ef61fbfa4348d0529", "8fcb4d3d4df61719ee3da98241393779290e0efcd88a49e363e2a2dfbc04dae9", "de584703c78a60a56028f9834086facd1401b355", "dbe51eabebf9d4ef9581ef99844a2944", "0ff6abe0252d4f37a196a1231fae5f26", "410eddfc19de44249897986ecc8ac449") or MD5 in~ ("9a10e1faa86a5d39417cae44da5adf38824dfb9a16432e34df766aa1dc9e3525", "07c69fc33271cf5a2ce03ac1fed7a3b16357aec093c5bf9ef61fbfa4348d0529", "8fcb4d3d4df61719ee3da98241393779290e0efcd88a49e363e2a2dfbc04dae9", "de584703c78a60a56028f9834086facd1401b355", "dbe51eabebf9d4ef9581ef99844a2944", "0ff6abe0252d4f37a196a1231fae5f26", "410eddfc19de44249897986ecc8ac449")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9a10e1faa86a5d39417cae44da5adf38824dfb9a16432e34df766aa1dc9e3525", "07c69fc33271cf5a2ce03ac1fed7a3b16357aec093c5bf9ef61fbfa4348d0529", "8fcb4d3d4df61719ee3da98241393779290e0efcd88a49e363e2a2dfbc04dae9", "de584703c78a60a56028f9834086facd1401b355", "dbe51eabebf9d4ef9581ef99844a2944", "0ff6abe0252d4f37a196a1231fae5f26", "410eddfc19de44249897986ecc8ac449") or SHA1 in~ ("9a10e1faa86a5d39417cae44da5adf38824dfb9a16432e34df766aa1dc9e3525", "07c69fc33271cf5a2ce03ac1fed7a3b16357aec093c5bf9ef61fbfa4348d0529", "8fcb4d3d4df61719ee3da98241393779290e0efcd88a49e363e2a2dfbc04dae9", "de584703c78a60a56028f9834086facd1401b355", "dbe51eabebf9d4ef9581ef99844a2944", "0ff6abe0252d4f37a196a1231fae5f26", "410eddfc19de44249897986ecc8ac449") or MD5 in~ ("9a10e1faa86a5d39417cae44da5adf38824dfb9a16432e34df766aa1dc9e3525", "07c69fc33271cf5a2ce03ac1fed7a3b16357aec093c5bf9ef61fbfa4348d0529", "8fcb4d3d4df61719ee3da98241393779290e0efcd88a49e363e2a2dfbc04dae9", "de584703c78a60a56028f9834086facd1401b355", "dbe51eabebf9d4ef9581ef99844a2944", "0ff6abe0252d4f37a196a1231fae5f26", "410eddfc19de44249897986ecc8ac449")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9a10e1faa86a5d39417cae44da5adf38824dfb9a16432e34df766aa1dc9e3525", "07c69fc33271cf5a2ce03ac1fed7a3b16357aec093c5bf9ef61fbfa4348d0529", "8fcb4d3d4df61719ee3da98241393779290e0efcd88a49e363e2a2dfbc04dae9", "de584703c78a60a56028f9834086facd1401b355", "dbe51eabebf9d4ef9581ef99844a2944", "0ff6abe0252d4f37a196a1231fae5f26", "410eddfc19de44249897986ecc8ac449"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

NGINX CVE-2026-42945 Exploited in the Wild, Causing Worker Crashes and Possible RCE

The Hacker News
2026-05-17 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A newly disclosed security flaw impacting NGINX Plus and NGINX Open has come under active exploitation in the wild, days after its public disclosure, according to VulnCheck. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-42945 (CVSS score: 9.2), is a heap buffer overflow in ngx_http_rewrite_module affecting NGINX versions 0.6.27 through 1.30.0. [LLM] openDCIM report_network_map.php 'dot' Parameter OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-28517) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of openDCIM CVE-2026-28517 — an unsanitised 'dot' parameter on /report_network_map.php that's passed directly to a shell. Hunts requests that combine the specific endpoint, the specific parameter, and shell-metacharacter payloads, matching the active in-the-wild exploitation observed by VulnCheck. Rationale: Article names the exact vulnerable component ('report_network_map.php'), exact parameter ('dot') and exact behaviour (parameter passed directly to a shell command). Combining endpoint + param + shell metacharacters is high-fidelity because legitimate dot/graphviz syntax does not normally include backticks, $( or pipe characters.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in ("F5","Imperva","Cloudflare","Fortinet","Citrix","Akamai","AWS","Palo Alto Networks","Barracuda") or DeviceProduct has_any ("WAF","Web Application Firewall","ASM","ModSecurity")
| where RequestURL has "report_network_map.php"
| where RequestURL has_any ("dot=", "dot%3D", "%64%6F%74=")
| where RequestURL has_any (";", "|", "`", "$(", "%3B", "%7C", "%60", "%24%28", "&&", "%26%26")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationServiceName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Web Server Process Spawning Shell or Network Tool (openDCIM / NGINX Post-Exploit) Installation High
Detects php-fpm / php-cgi / nginx / apache spawning a shell or network-egress LOLBin — the post-exploitation tell-tale for the openDCIM 5-request RCE chain and any NGINX CVE-2026-42945 RCE attempt. Article-specific because both vulnerabilities terminate in a reverse shell or wget/curl staging step running under the web-server uid. Rationale: Article describes a chain that 'spawn a reverse shell' over five HTTP requests and drops a PHP web shell. A child shell/curl/wget under php-fpm or nginx parent on a Linux host is the unambiguous signature; both CVE-2026-42945 RCE (where ASLR is disabled) and the openDCIM chain land here.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm","php-cgi","php","php7.4","php8.0","php8.1","php8.2","httpd","apache2","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","curl","wget","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","busybox")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"/(sh|bash|dash|zsh|curl|wget|python3?|perl|nc|ncat|socat|busybox)$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] NGINX Worker Process SIGSEGV Crash Burst (CVE-2026-42945 DoS Indicator) Exploitation Medium
Detects clusters of NGINX worker-process abnormal terminations (SIGSEGV / signal 11) — the directly-observable signal of CVE-2026-42945 heap-buffer-overflow exploitation against ngx_http_rewrite_module. Even on ASLR-enabled hosts where RCE is unreliable, the worker crash is exploitable and triggers this telemetry on every attempt. Rationale: Article quotes AlmaLinux maintainers calling the 'worker-crash DoS exploitable enough on its own' and VulnCheck observing active exploitation. ngx_http_rewrite_module heap overflow corrupts the worker heap and produces SIGSEGV/SIGABRT in nginx error logs — the cleanest signal for this CVE that doesn't require either successful RCE or the attacker knowing the right config.
ATT&CKT1499.004 T1190
Data sourcesApplication_State
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName == "nginx" or SyslogMessage has "nginx"
| where SyslogMessage has "worker process"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("exited on signal 11","exited on signal 6","SIGSEGV","SIGABRT","core dumped")
| summarize CrashCount = count(), SampleMsgs = make_set(SyslogMessage, 5), WorkerPids = make_set(extract(@"worker process (\d+)", 1, SyslogMessage), 25) by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where CrashCount >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.syslog "worker process" ("exited on signal 11" OR "exited on signal 6" OR SIGSEGV OR SIGABRT OR "core dumped") nginx
APPLICATION
search index=* sourcetype IN ("nginx:error","nginx_error","syslog") ("worker process" AND ("exited on signal 11" OR "exited on signal 6" OR "SIGSEGV" OR "SIGABRT" OR "core dumped")) | rex field=_raw "worker process (?<pid>\d+) exited on signal (?<signal>\d+)" | bin _time span=5m | stats count as crash_count, values(signal) as signals, values(pid) as worker_pids, values(host) as hosts by _time host | where crash_count >= 3 | sort - _time
[LLM] PHP Web Shell Drop in openDCIM / Web-Server Document Root Installation High
Detects creation of .php/.phtml/.phar files inside openDCIM or generic web document roots, written by a web-server process (php-fpm, nginx, apache). VulnCheck explicitly observed the actor dropping a PHP web shell after exploiting the openDCIM chain; the web-server-user-writing-PHP-to-webroot pattern is the cleanest tell. Rationale: VulnCheck quote: actor 'dropping a PHP web shell' after Vulnhuntr-based exploit chain. A web-server-uid process writing a new .php file into a document root is one of the highest-signal webshell-drop patterns; combined with openDCIM-specific paths it pinpoints this campaign.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/opendcim/","/var/www/","/srv/www/","/usr/share/opendcim","/usr/share/nginx/","/etc/nginx/html/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("nginx","php-fpm","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","php")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc
